title: Telugu-Only Audio Platform Kavi Launches for Global Diaspora Listeners
excerpt: Kavi Media's Telugu-only service pairs licensed titles with originals across podcasts, audiobooks and short-form "Bites," aimed at Telugu speakers worldwide on monthly and annual plans.
body:
• Kavi Media Inc. has launched Kavi, a streaming platform and production house carrying audiobooks, podcasts, audio shows and short-form audio exclusively in Telugu.
  • Founder and CEO Srihith Pallamreddy built the company after finding Telugu creators and listeners scattered across general platforms with no dedicated home.
  • The catalogue mixes licensed titles with Kavi Originals — podcasts, audiobooks, original serials, independent music and sub-90-second "Bites" — on monthly and annual subscriptions; the company says it expects to double its library within weeks.
  • Kavi raised a $150,000 pre-seed round earlier this year, with $53,000 committed at the time it was announced in May.

Telugu listeners abroad have a new address. Kavi Media Inc. has officially launched Kavi, a platform that brings together audiobooks, podcasts, audio shows and short-form audio content exclusively in Telugu, The American Bazaar reported.

Kavi is built as both a production house and a streaming platform, aiming to connect storytellers, artists and subject-matter experts with audiences who want entertainment in their own language. Its catalogue combines licensed content with Kavi Originals, with exclusive releases and early access to select titles.

What is on it

The library spans podcasts — conversations, interviews, comedy and storytelling — audiobooks of novels, short stories and poetry, and original episodic audio series including family dramas, comedy serials and documentaries. It also carries independent music from Telugu artists, including non-film tracks, audio designed for relaxation and focus, and a short-form category called "Bites": sketches, moments and highlights lasting less than 90 seconds. The platform is designed for a global Telugu-speaking audience and offers monthly and annual subscription options; the launch announcement did not publish prices.

"We're really focused on providing the platform and support that Telugu audio creators never had. Inherently, that allows us to build a great platform for Telugu listeners to just unwind and listen."

— Srihith Pallamreddy, CEO and founder of Kavi

Why a Telugu-only platform

Pallamreddy founded Kavi after identifying a gap in the regional audio market: Telugu creators and listeners were spread across multiple general platforms without a central destination built for Telugu storytelling. The company announced in May that it was raising a $150,000 pre-seed round, structured as a Y Combinator SAFE agreement, with $53,000 already committed — money intended to expand the library and build creator partnerships and monetisation tools ahead of launch.

What happens next

"We're launching today with Telugu podcasts, stories and shows, and this is just the start," the company said. "New titles are landing every couple of days, and we expect to double our library in the next couple of weeks." Kavi says it plans to keep expanding its original programming and creator partnerships. For Telugu-speaking households in the US and elsewhere in the diaspora — where the language's film music is easy to stream but its stories, serials and audiobooks have had no single home — the test will be whether the catalogue grows fast enough, and deep enough, to make a dedicated subscription worth keeping. Listeners, creators and potential partners can explore the platform through Kavi's website, the company said.
image_caption: The Kavi app on smartphones, showing its podcast home screen and episode player. Kavi Media launched the Telugu-only audio platform for a global audience in November 2026.
